children: CATCH-TB has been selected for funding within the European Partnership on One Health Antimicrobial Resistance, EUP OHAMR. The project builds on the research behind ZymIQ Biopharma’s enzyme platform Mycolyse and brings together research groups in Sweden, Germany, Portugal and South Africa. With a total project budget of EUR 1.65 million over three years, the consortium will investigate enzyme-based adjunctive treatments that may enhance the effect of antibiotics against drug resistant tuberculosis.
A new approach to combating antibiotic resistance

Antibiotic resistance is one of the greatest global threats to human health. Tuberculosis is one of the world’s most serious infectious diseases. According to WHO, around 10.6 million people fell ill in 2025 and approximately 1.13 million died.

Tuberculosis bacteria belong to the group of mycobacteria. Their complex cell wall and ability to survive inside the body’s cells make treatment difficult. Antibiotic resistance complicates it further and increases the need for new treatment options.
Mycolyse is based on engineered enzymes that attack the protective cell wall structures of mycobacteria. The aim is both to kill bacteria and to improve the ability of antibiotics to act.
Research results provide a basis for the next step
The research behind Mycolyse was published in 2026 in
Trends in Biotechnology

. The autors include, Dr Adel Abouhmad, Jana Kassaliete and Dr Mats Clarsund, all of ZymIQ Biopharma, together with researchers at Lund University and international partners. It demonstrates antibacterial activity against several mycobacterial species, activity in infected cells and efficacy in initial animal models. The researchers also report a synergistic effect in combination with rifampicin.

The results also cover nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM), which can cause lung infections that are difficult to treat. The potential of Mycolyse therefore extends beyond tuberculosis. The research has also been highlighted in a separate scientific commentary in the same journal.
In addition to the published results, ZymIQ has demonstrated antibacterial activity against
Mycobacterium tuberculosis
, the main cause of tuberculosis. These results have not yet been published.

CATCH-TB will build on these results, with a particular focus on drug resistant tuberculosis bacteria and combinations with established antibiotics. The project also covers delivery to infected cells, both of the enzymes themselves and of mRNA that instructs the cells to produce the enzymes.
International consortium with complementary expertise

The project is coordinated by Professor Rajni Hatti Kaul at Lund University. The consortium combines expertise in enzyme design, tuberculosis and resistance mechanisms with mRNA technology, drug formulation and industrial development:
Lund University (Professor Rajni Hatti Kaul):
project coordination, enzyme technology and protein design.
Forschungszentrum Borstel, Germany (Professor Stefan Niemann):
tuberculosis, clinical bacterial strains and resistance.
University of Rostock, Germany (Dr Moritz Jansson):
mRNA based antibacterial treatments.
University of Lisbon, Portugal (Professor António Almeida):
drug formulation and delivery systems.
Stellenbosch University/SU SAMRC, South Africa (Professor Mohlopheni Marakalala):
tuberculosis research and advanced infection models.
ZymIQ Biopharma (Dr Mats Clarsund):
the company’s enzyme-based drug candidates (Mycolyse), patent protection and responsibility for further development towards clinical trials.
A basis for further development and collaboration

“CATCH-TB strengthens the development of our enzyme-based drug candidates. Together with the consortium, we will select which candidates and treatment combinations should be taken forward. ZymIQ Biopharma’s role is to drive further development towards clinical trials and to build collaborations with pharmaceutical companies,” says Dr Mats Clarsund, CTO of ZymIQ Biopharma.
ZymIQ Biopharma welcomes dialogue with research and industry partners on the further development of Mycolyse.
ZymIQ contributes its own research and development efforts. The public project funding goes to the academic partners and does not involve any direct project grant to ZymIQ.
The news is presented in connection with World AMR Awareness Week, 18 to 24 November. This year’s theme is “
One Health, one action: Prevent AMR now

About ZymIQ Biopharma

ZymIQ Biopharma AB is a Swedish biotechnology company within the ZymIQ Group, based in Lund. The company develops enzyme-based and immunomodulatory technologies against infections. Its programmes include Mycolyse for mycobacterial infections and Stapholyse for staphylococcal infections.
